record.original_question: Characterize those Scott sober dcpos P for which, for every Scott sober dcpo Q, the product P x Q is again Scott sober.

evidence.quote: Question 4.8. Characterize those Scott sober dcpos P for which the products P x Q is Scott sober for every Scott sober dcpo Q.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a directed-complete partial order (dcpo), i.e., a poset in which every directed subset has a supremum. The Scott topology on $P$ has as open sets those upper sets $U \subseteq P$ such that whenever a directed set $D \subseteq P$ has $\sup D \in U$, then $D \cap U \neq \emptyset$. Write $\Sigma P$ for $P$ equipped with the Scott topology. A topological space $X$ is called sober if every nonempty irreducible closed subset (a nonempty closed set that is not the union of two proper closed subsets) is the closure of a unique singleton. A dcpo $P$ is said to be Scott sober if $\Sigma P$ is sober.

Given two dcpos $P$ and $Q$, their product $P \times Q$ is the dcpo with the coordinatewise order; its Scott topology is in general finer than the product of the Scott topologies on $P$ and $Q$.

Problem: Give an order-theoretic characterization of those Scott sober dcpos $P$ with the following property — for every Scott sober dcpo $Q$, the product dcpo $P \times Q$ (equipped with its Scott topology) is again Scott sober.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., a 2024 preprint titled "Products of two sober dcpo's need not be sober") confirms that products of Scott sober dcpos can fail to be Scott sober and gives partial sufficient conditions for special classes (e.g., certain sober complete lattices), but no general order-theoretic characterization of the class of Scott sober dcpos $P$ for which $P \times Q$ is Scott sober for every Scott sober $Q$ appears to be known. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Products of two sober dcpo's need not be sober
status_evidence.snippet: Two dcpo's whose Scott spaces are sober can have an order product whose Scott space is not sober.
status_evidence.claim: Sobriety of Scott topology is not preserved under arbitrary products of sober dcpos, so a nontrivial characterization is needed.

status_evidence.title: On sobriety of Scott topology on dcpos
status_evidence.snippet: An important open problem asks for an order-theoretic characterization of dcpos which are sober with respect to their Scott topology.
status_evidence.claim: Order-theoretic characterizations related to Scott sobriety remain open.
